subject: Approval request: Private Offer — EU geo split, upfront credit, and SLA carveout
messages:
From: Sarah Chung <sarah.chung@nimbusdw.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-23 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Private offer request — EU-only listing, commission split and credit

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Nimbus Dataworks would like to proceed with a private offer on AWS Marketplace that is EU-only (we're subject to data residency constraints). A few non-standard items they're asking for:

- 40% rev-share in year 1 (then 30% thereafter)
- $150k upfront platform credit applied against first invoice
- SLA carveout: 99.5% uptime target instead of standard 99.9% for the first 12 months, with capped SLA credit at 10% of monthly invoice
- Net90 payment terms and invoice grouping for multi-region billing (we'll only list EU, but procurement prefers consolidated invoicing)

I've attached the RFP and their proposed term sheet. They asked whether Redwood can make this an AWS private offer and whether Marketplace will accept the commission structure + upfront credit. Time is tight — they want to close by end of September.

Can you let me know next steps and whether you need anything else from our side?

Thanks,
Sarah Chung
Head of Alliances, Nimbus Dataworks
Attachments: Nimbus_RFP_Q3.pdf (pdf), Proposed_Term_Sheet.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-24 11:03:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Private offer request — EU-only listing, commission split and credit

Karthik — forwarding Nimbus' ask and attached term sheet. Summary and recommended immediate asks: 

Summary of external ask (from Sarah):
- EU-only AWS private offer
- Rev-share: 40% year 1, 30% thereafter
- $150k upfront credit applied to first invoice
- SLA lowered to 99.5% for first 12 months with a 10% cap on credits
- Net90 payment terms

Deal Desk review needed: can we accept 40% rev-share year 1 + $150k credit? Also need guidance on SLA carveout language (product impact) and whether AWS Marketplace will permit combined upfront credit + higher rev-share in the same private offer.

Business context: Nimbus is a mid-enterprise account, strong reference potential in EU public sector. This is a strategic entry for us into their EU procurement ecosystem; if we concede too much on economics now it sets a precedent but losing them would be a blow to pipeline. They want to finalize by 2027-09-30.

Ask from me to you / Marissa:
- Karthik: please provide Deal Desk econ impact (ARR dilution, payback, one-time cost) and a recommended counter (if any).
- Marissa: need exec approval if Deal Desk recommends any deviation from standard commission floors or >$100k upfront credits or Net90.
- Markus: legal review for SLA carveout exposure and required indemnities.

Attachments: Proposed_Term_Sheet.xlsx, DealDesk_Econ_Model.csv

Can you respond by EOD 2027-09-24? Nimbus will escalate if we delay.

—Olga
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-24 15:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private offer request — EU-only listing, commission split and credit

Thanks for the summary, Olga. Quick Deal Desk analysis below. I also attached a simple econ model (DealDesk_Econ_Model.csv) with two scenarios.

Key inputs / assumptions:
- Expected year 1 billings to Marketplace: $750k (customer estimate)
- Standard rev-share: 30%
- Proposed rev-share: 40% Y1 (delta = 10% = additional pay to partner)
- Upfront credit requested: $150k applied to first invoice

Scenario A (accept as requested):
- Year 1 Marketplace gross to Redwood: $750k * (1 - 0.40) = $450k
- With $150k credit applied, Redwood collection in Y1 = $300k (one-time hit)
- Effective ARR recognized Y1 materially reduced; payback for CAC extended

Scenario B (counter recommended):
- Rev-share 35% Y1 (compromise), revert to 30% Y2+
- Upfront credit $75k conditioned on a 12-month minimum purchase commitment of $600k billed through marketplace
- SLA: agree to 99.5% for first 6 months only, then standard 99.9% afterward; keep credit cap at 10% monthly invoice but require performance milestones to trigger extension
- Payment terms: propose Net45 instead of Net90; or Net90 only if Nimbus signs a DPA amendment and a 12-month committed spend schedule

Recommendation: pursue Scenario B and escalate only if Marissa wants to make a strategic concession to drive EU reference quickly. 40% + $150k is above our usual tolerance without a long-term commitment; this will materially reduce short-term cash.

Time sensitivity: if we want to close by 9/30 we need exec decision today or tomorrow morning. If approved, I will prepare a conditional term sheet for AWS private offer intake.

—Karthik
Head of Deal Desk
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-25 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private offer request — EU-only listing, commission split and credit

Appreciate the quick analysis. I agree with Karthik's Scenario B with the following executive signoffs and conditions:

1) Rev-share: approve 35% for year 1, revert to 30% for year 2+.
2) Upfront credit: $75k, only with an executed 12-month minimum committed spend of $600k billed via Marketplace (documented in the private offer or an attached SOW).
3) SLA: accept 99.5% for first 6 months only. Cap SLA credits at 10% monthly invoice. Any extension beyond 6 months requires a written operational remediation plan and sign-off from Markus/legal.
4) Payment terms: Net45 standard; Net90 only if Procurement (Nimbus) signs the DPA amendment and commit schedule.
5) EU-only listing is acceptable, but Ops must confirm region tagging and billing grouping will work for consolidated invoicing. Olga, please coordinate with Marketplace Ops (aws-marketplace-ops@amazon.com) as needed.

Markus — please draft a short amendment capturing the SLA carveout, the upfront credit conditions, and the committed spend schedule. Keep liability language standard; do not expand indemnities.

Karthik — proceed to prepare the conditional private offer payload for AWS (35%/75k credit/commitment language). If Nimbus pushes for 40% or full $150k, escalate back to me with quantified reference benefit and expected incremental ARR.

Olga — let Nimbus know we can move forward under these terms and request they sign the commitment schedule. Push to close but do not concede Net90 or larger credit without the signed commitment.

Marissa
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
